prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can you recommend a really popular wine for under 25 euros that everyone likes, tastes a bit sweet and peppery with cherry flavors, isn't too heavy, and is nice for drinking on a cold winter night?"

List A:
Wine 1: Grenache, Australia, $13. Tasting note: "This round, soft, alcoholic wine deserves praise for its spicy-peppery warmth and abundant cherry fruit. Those same qualities are also its biggest shortcoming: The low acidity and high alcohol make it seem a bit heavy. —J.C"
Wine 2: Merlot, US, $19. Tasting note: "A modest wine that has much to be modest about. It's dry and rather simple, with candied cherry-berry, cola and spice flavors."
Wine 3: Petite Sirah, US, $11. Tasting note: "With sweet berry, cherry and spice flavors, this is a fine wine for drinking now with everyday fare. It's soft and a little sweet, with bracing tannins."
Wine 4: Meritage, US, $18. Tasting note: "Here's a rich, smooth wine for drinking now. It's softly luscious, packed with blackberry, cherry, anise and cedar flavors that finish with quite a bit of complexity."
Wine 5: Aglianico, Italy, $94. Tasting note: "Here's a modern and beautiful wine with warming tones of vanilla, spice, chocolate and blackberry. The wine is thick and dense with dark extraction and very solid tannins. Drink after 2010. A Marc de Grazia selection, various American importers."

List B:
Wine 1: Montepulciano, Italy, $16. Tasting note: "Here is a ripe but well-balanced wine with aromas of cherry, spice, dark chocolate and minerals. The wine boasts a modern edge that is identified by its soft, forthcoming personality and its jammy fruit characteristics. It tastes smooth and rich and would pair with any hearty winter meal."
Wine 2: Cabernet Franc, US, $20. Tasting note: "A very easy wine to like. It's so softly balanced, so rich in cherries, licorice and smoky vanilla, so light in texture, you could drink it as a cocktail wine. But it will also nicely complement a wide variety of foods."
Wine 3: Rosé, US, $16. Tasting note: "A little too heavy and full-bodied for a blush, this wine has flavors of melted cherry jam, vanilla, oatmeal cookies and pepper. It's a good wine, but could use greater delicacy and charm."
Wine 4: Pinot Noir, US, $20. Tasting note: "It's rare to get a twenty buck Pinot Noir this good. The wine is dry, silky and elegant, almost faultless in its precision. With savory cherry, red licorice, cola and sandalwood flavors, it's not an ager, but a very pretty wine for drinking now."
Wine 5: Merlot, US, $28. Tasting note: "Don't look for density or any particular varietal focus here, but what you will find is a pleasing, soft, smooth wine with black cherry, licorice, smoke and chocolate. It's all front-loaded and fruit-driven, but if you want something to enjoy right now, preferably outdoors, with some butterfat in the soft, pliable tannins, this wine will deliver the goods."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
